title: Peking Duck
subtitle: Lacquered roast duck with crispy skin
excerpt: Whole duck air-dried overnight to tighten the skin, then roasted at high heat until the skin is shatteringly crisp and mahogany red. Served the traditional way: sliced at the table and wrapped in thin pancakes with spring onion, cucumber, and hoisin sauce.

recipe.sourceNotes: Peking duck (北京烤鸭) is one of China's most celebrated dishes, with a history documented from the Imperial era; it appears in court records of the Yuan Dynasty (1271 to 1368) and became a speciality of the restaurants surrounding the Forbidden City in Beijing. The defining technique is the preparation before roasting: the skin is separated from the flesh by inflating air beneath it, the bird is blanched, then lacquered with a maltose or honey glaze, and hung to air-dry for at least 24 hours. This removes surface moisture and tightens the skin so it can render and crisp completely during the high-heat roast. The traditional serving — skin with a tiny sliver of meat, wrapped in a thin pancake with spring onion and hoisin — is the canonical form; the remaining meat is used in a second course.

content.text: The air-drying step cannot be skipped. It is what makes Peking duck different from ordinary roast duck. At minimum 24 hours uncovered in the fridge; 48 hours gives a noticeably better skin. The duck must sit on a rack over a tray so air circulates all around it. Do not cover it.

items.preparation: use a whole duck instead; approximately 2 kg
mixed with 1 tbsp hot water for the glaze
cut into fine strips; to serve

content.text: Pat the duck dry inside and out. Place the star anise and cinnamon inside the cavity. Mix the honey, soy sauce, and vinegar. Brush all over the duck. Place on a rack over a tray and refrigerate uncovered for 24 to 48 hours, brushing with the glaze once or twice more during drying.

Heat the oven to 220°C / fan 200°C / gas 7. Season the duck with salt. Roast breast-side up for 20 minutes. Reduce the heat to 180°C / fan 160°C / gas 4 and roast for a further 60 to 70 minutes until the skin is deep mahogany and crisp and the juices run clear when the thigh is pierced.

Rest the duck for 10 minutes. Carve the skin and meat into thin slices. Serve with warm Chinese pancakes or flour tortillas, spring onion strips, cucumber strips, and hoisin sauce for dipping. Each person assembles their own wraps at the table.
